// diagnostic

E3401

`{pure_fn}` calls the impure function `{call}`.

What

`{pure_fn}` calls the impure function `{call}`.

Why

A `fn … -[]>` may only call functions whose effect row is empty, declared or inferred, and pure builtins. Impure calls make the result non-deterministic. In `jet eval --pure` the whole call graph from `run` is checked transitively; the why-line shows the full chain (`run → a → b calls \`print\``) so the user can find the leak. Compile-time work (`#run` blocks and values) shares this same call-graph walk: the message reads `{call}` is not allowed in comptime code instead, since there is no enclosing `-[]>` function name to report.

Fix

Remove the call from `{pure_fn}`, or drop the `-[]>` bound from `{pure_fn}` so its effects are inferred; at compile time, compute the value at runtime instead.

Worked example

First UI snapshot mentioning E3401: Tests/UI/Effects/pure_fn_with_core_effect_is_e3401.stderr.

Error [jet.ImpureCallInPureContext]: `readit` calls the impure function `files.read`
  --> Tests/UI/Effects/pure_fn_with_core_effect_is_e3401.jet:3:47
    |
  3 | readit: fn(p: String) -[]> String { return fs.read(p) ?? "" }
    |                                               ^^^^
 Why: `files.read` is impure, but `readit` declares `-[]>`
 Fix: Remove the call from `readit`, or drop the `-[]>` bound from `readit` so its effects are inferred
 Denial: pure
 Call chain: readit → files.read
